title: super-board skill map
subtitle: Skeleton generated by visual.py skillmap — enrich what/when/how

nodes.label: /super-board
nodes.what: Orchestrator: plans waves, runs Build → QA → Review, merges when green.
nodes.when: Use when the user says "super-board", "/super-board", "drain my GitHub project", "set up the autonomous loop", "kick off the headless build/QA pipeline", or "stop super-board".
nodes.how: If invoked with no verb, ask which one.

nodes.label: /super-board onboard
nodes.what: one-time setup wizard; writes .claude/super-board/configs/<slug>.json

nodes.label: /super-board lint
nodes.what: walks active-pipeline issues, flags vague ACs, runs pre-flight readiness

nodes.label: /super-board status
nodes.what: snapshot of active config, column counts, in-flight workers

nodes.label: /super-board run
nodes.what: the autonomous loop: waves of the super-board-wave dynamic workflow, run from this session (worker_backend: "claude-p" opts into the legacy headless runner .claude/bin/super-board-run.sh). Also the resume command — state lives on the board, not in process memory. Accepts a model-tier flag: --low (ha

nodes.label: /super-board stop
nodes.what: graceful shutdown: posts "stopped mid-flight" comments on every in-flight issue + PR, releases assignee mutexes, kills workers + dispatcher. Next super-board run resumes.

nodes.label: super-build
nodes.what: Builder lane: worktree, smallest safe change, tests, draft PR.
nodes.when: Use when the user says "Super Build", "run the build loop", "/super-build", or invokes the skill.
nodes.how: Inside `super-board run`, Super Build is the Builder lane: a lane agent in the in-session wave workflow (`workflows/super-board-wave.js`) that follows "super-board integration" below. Run on its own, `/super-build` is the **legacy headless path (opt-in)**: you are the orchestrator, the source of truth is the **`Ready` column of the configured GitHub Project board**, and your job is to dispatch eve

nodes.label: /super-collect
nodes.what: Finds problems (Sentry, PostHog, issues, PRs, architecture) and files verified Backlog cards.
nodes.when: Use when the user says "super-collect", "/super-collect", "/super-collect sentry", "collect tickets", "triage errors onto the board", "what keeps breaking", or "find refactors".
nodes.how: One job: find problems and file tickets into the board's **Backlog**. The board fixes them. super-collect never builds, never edits app code, and never moves a card to `Ready` — `super-board lint` decides that. Per project only: it reads the active project's super-board config and files onto that project's board.

nodes.label: super-qa
nodes.what: Tester lane: evidence, test-gap check, screenshots, or bounce to Build.
nodes.when: Use when the user says "run super-qa", "QA review", "bug bash", "verify and fix", or invokes `/super-qa`.
nodes.how: Before iter 1, resolve a test login. **Never ask the user; discover or create.** Order:

nodes.label: super-review
nodes.what: Reviewer lane: own hypotheses, remembers prior findings, merge gate.
nodes.when: Use when the user says "Super Review", "review this branch", "review loop", "make sure this is merge-ready", "PR review", or asks for code, architecture, security, QA evidence, or release-readiness judgment.
nodes.how: **Super Review** is the super-board reviewer. It checks whether a branch or PR is safe to merge, records actionable findings, and routes fixes to the right Super workflow.

nodes.label: /ui-refine-loop
nodes.what: Critique → refine loop that polishes one page or component.
nodes.when: Use when the user says "ui-refine-loop", "/ui-refine-loop", "refine loop", "iterate on this page", "polish this page with impeccable", or "keep polishing".
nodes.how: Impeccable's `critique` and `audit` find problems once, and each fix command (`distill`, `layout`, `polish`, and the rest) fixes one kind once. This skill chains them into a short unattended loop. Each round, **fresh checkers** find and rank the problems, then a **fresh fixer** picks the right Impeccable commands and lands one green commit. A short ledger is the only thing carried between rounds,

nodes.label: /visual
nodes.what: One HTML page: branch recap, plan, or codebase map with diagrams.
nodes.when: Use when the user runs /visual or asks to visualise, picture, or visually recap a branch, PR, diff, plan, or part of a codebase.
nodes.how: One command, one page. You write a `data.json`; `scripts/visual.py render` injects it into `assets/template.html`, which draws everything inline (SVG diagrams, file map, diffs) with no build step and no runtime CDN. Paths below are relative to this skill's folder; run the script from inside the project being visualised.

nodes.label: code-review
nodes.what: Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes — Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/spec asked for?).
nodes.when: Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to "review since X".

nodes.label: codebase-design

nodes.when: Use when the user wants to design or improve a module's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or AI-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary.

nodes.label: diagnosing-bugs

nodes.when: Use when the user says "diagnose"/"debug this", or reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow.

nodes.when: Use when about to claim work is complete, fixed, or passing, before committing or creating PRs - requires running verification commands and confirming output before making any success claims; evidence before assertions always

nodes.label: tdd-v2
nodes.what: The EricOS testing ladder — which rung a test belongs at and what must be true before climbing to the next.
nodes.when: Use when writing any test, building a feature test-first, or choosing between a unit test, a component test, and a browser end-to-end spec. Supersedes any other TDD skill here; pairs with `tdd`, which owns the red-green discipline.

nodes.label: ponytail-review
nodes.what: Review a diff for over-engineering.

nodes.label: humanizer
nodes.what: Strip AI writing tells from any draft so it reads like a person wrote it.
nodes.when: Use when writing or rewriting emails, Skool posts, lessons, scripts, docs, or any prose Eric will publish or send, and when he says humanize, make this sound human, less AI, remove the AI tells, or de-slop this. Runs as a pass over a finished draft, with Eric Tech overrides so bold, bullets and emoji survive.

nodes.label: impeccable
nodes.what: Use when the user wants to design, redesign, shape, critique, audit, polish, clarify, distill, harden, optimize, adapt, animate, colorize, extract, or otherwise improve a frontend interface.
nodes.when: Use when the user wants to design, redesign, shape, critique, audit, polish, clarify, distill, harden, optimize, adapt, animate, colorize, extract, or otherwise improve a frontend interface. Covers websites, landing pages, dashboards, product UI, app shells, components, forms, settings, onboarding, and empty states. Handles UX review, visual hierarchy, information architecture, cognitive load, accessibility, performance, responsive behavior, theming, anti-patterns, typography, fonts, spacing, layout, alignment, color, motion, micro-interactions, UX copy, error states, edge cases, i18n, and reusable design systems or tokens. Also use for bland designs that need to become bolder or more delightful, loud designs that should become quieter, live browser iteration on UI elements, or ambitious visual effects that should feel technically extraordinary. Not for backend-only or non-UI tasks.
